messages:
incident-bot: Pager: CRITICAL - Prod runtime pods entering CrashLoopBackOff on cluster prod-gpu-2. Affected deployment: inference/redwood-infer-v2 (tensorrt-llm variant). Error: SIGSEGV in runtime_engine.so. See alerts: https://ops.redwood/alerts/INC-4182 :rotating_light:

maria.nguyen: I'm oncall. seeing 50+ crashlooping pods across 3 nodes, traffic errors 502 -> elevated errors to customers. Rolling paging to eng-runtime-oncall and SRE.

samir.rao: Joining. quick check - are these all same kernel/driver? I see pattern: pods crash during model load, stacktrace hits fused-kernel path.

priya.patel: Logs attached from one pod: ```
[2026-03-15T01:07:12Z] runtime_engine: loading model tensorrt-llm v3.2.1
[2026-03-15T01:07:12Z] runtime_engine: init_fused_kernels() -> 0x7f8abf...
[2026-03-15T01:07:12Z] runtime_engine: ERROR: segfault at 0x00000000 (signal 11)
#0 0x7f8abf4f in fused_op_exec+0x1f
#1 0x7f8ac0a2 in load_model+0x4a
```

devon: Reproduced locally with model weight set and quantization profile Q4. Failure looks like fused kernel code path calling a null ptr.

eng-runtime-oncall: Oncall here. I can confirm backtraces from two different nodes show same crash site inside fused kernel. Likely regression from runtime image `redwood/runtime:2026-03-14-09a2b3`.

oncall-sre: Customer-facing impact: ~3% of token generation requests returned 502/504 over last 15m, concentrated on region us-west2. No data loss, only availability degradations.

maria.nguyen: Mitigation plan per runbook: 1) Stop new rollouts to that image. 2) Route traffic away from affected nodes/pods. 3) Enable fallback model (redwood-infer-v2-cpu-fallback) for latency-tolerant routes. 4) Attempt quick hotpatch: disable fused kernels via env var.

samir.rao: Running commands now: ```
# cordon and drain problematic nodes
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12.us-west2
kubectl drain gpu-node-12.us-west2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```

priya.patel: Setting env on deployment to disable fused kernels: ```yaml
- name: RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED_KERNELS
  value: "1"
```
Applying rollout: `kubectl set env deploy/redwood-infer-v2 RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED_KERNELS=1`

eng-runtime-oncall: Patch applied. Triggering rolling restart with increased restartBackoff. Monitor logs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for deploy/redwood-infer-v2 @sha:2026-03-14-09a2b3 -> env RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED_KERNELS=1

maria.nguyen: Observing immediate reduction in crashloop counts: from 52 -> 8 in 10m. Error rate fell to ~0.8% for affected routes. Good temporary mitigation.

devon: Quick root cause notes: the fused-kernel code path assumes an aligned pointer returned by the CUDA allocator. New allocator in driver nv-520.* can return different alignment; we hit null deref in a boundary condition.

samir.rao: For complete mitigation we should either roll back to previous runtime image or release a runtime hotfix that guards the pointer and avoids fused path on affected hardware.

eng-runtime-oncall: I'm building a hotfix branch now to skip fused kernels when alignment check fails and add a defensive null check. Will test on staging.

maria.nguyen: Customer comms: drafting a short notice - we should tell affected customers we saw transient 5xx errors for a small fraction of requests in us-west2, we routed traffic and applied a temporary configuration to stop the crashes. ETA for full fix TBD.

priya.patel: I pushed a quick rollback option: `kubectl set image deploy/redwood-infer-v2=redwood/runtime:2026-03-10-1b2c3d --record` in case hotfix tests fail.

eng-runtime-oncall: Hotfix built and running in canary (1 pod) in staging. Basic smoke tests pass (model load + sample inference). Pushing to canary in prod next.

maria.nguyen: Canary in prod started: 1 pod on us-west2 with hotfix image `redwood/runtime:hotfix-2026-03-15-01`. Monitoring telemetry.

oncall-sre: Telemetry: canary shows no segfaults for 40m and latency stable. Rolling to remaining pods in region with 5m pause between pods.

samir.rao: While rolling, please ensure core dumps are captured for pods that still crash so we can post-mortem. Commands to enable: `echo /opt/artifacts/core.%e.%p > /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern` inside node or use container runtime config.

priya.patel: Captured core from one failed pod and uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/INC-4182/core-20260315-01.gz. GDB backtrace attached to ticket.

eng-runtime-oncall: Hotfix rollout complete. All crashloops cleared, pod count stable. No further 502 spikes. Rolling back temporary env var not yet - will keep RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED_KERNELS=1 until we validate hotfix across hardware matrix.

maria.nguyen: Handoff at 02:56Z to follow-up shift. Summary for post-incident: cause: fused-kernel null-deref triggered by new allocator behaviour on nv-520 drivers. Mitigations: 1) immediate env var to disable fused kernels, 2) hotfix image deployed, 3) node cordon/drain for worst-hit hosts, 4) collected cores and traces, 5) customer comms drafted.

eng-runtime-oncall: Action items assigned: ENG-RUNTIME: complete regression fix and add alignment-check unit tests (#ticket-ENG-7892). SRE: add node-level health check that detects repeated segfaults and isolates nodes automatically. Support: send customer notifications and record affected customers list.

oncall-sre: Customer notification sent to impacted customers at 03:10Z. Follow-up planned after RCA.

maria.nguyen: Closing incident channel now; opening a postmortem thread and assigning owners. If any new crashes appear, reopen channel or page oncall. Thanks all. :pray:
